{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py",
      "line": 71,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Guard requests without an organization membership",
      "body": "Organization-scoped API authentication can authorize this endpoint without attaching a user membership, leaving organization_context.member as None. The new expression dereferences that member for non-superusers, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Previously working audit-log requests using organization API authentication will therefore return an AttributeError/500. Handle absent memberships and evaluate the optimization gate only for opt-in requests."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 840,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs",
      "body": "OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by=\"-datetime\", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime value to math.floor/math.ceil. Building cursors for any nonempty first page therefore raises TypeError. The inverse conversion also returns a raw numeric cursor value instead of the datetime required by the query. Inherit or reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new audit-log pagination path works."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 882,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Do not pass negative offsets to QuerySet slicing",
      "body": "The advanced-pagination branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds rather than interpreting them as reverse pagination, so an enabled request with a cursor such as 0:-1:0 raises an exception before fetching any rows. Implement reverse pagination using ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject unsupported offsets with a controlled pagination error."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",
      "line": 197,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Migrate or version the Redis buffer keyspace",
      "body": "This replaces Redis sets with sorted sets while retaining the existing span-buf:s:* key names. Live buffers written by the old consumer remain ordinary sets, so ZADD, ZCARD, and ZSCAN will raise WRONGTYPE after deployment. Failed processing batches cannot advance their Kafka offsets, and old and new consumers are mutually incompatible during a rolling upgrade. Introduce a compatible migration/drain strategy or a versioned buffer namespace before switching command types."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 47,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve timestamp scores when merging span buffers",
      "body": "Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. When the same payload is present in both buffers—for example, a replayed grandchild written under its parent after an earlier batch moved it to the root—its end-timestamp score is added to the existing score. An old span can consequently receive a score far beyond every real timestamp and survive eviction while newer spans are removed. Use a score-preserving aggregation such as AGGREGATE MAX for both unions."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Honor the configured maximum segment span count",
      "body": "The eviction threshold is hard-coded to 1000, while the Python flush-time check has been removed and SpansBuffer still exposes max_segment_spans. That constructor argument now has no effect: a configured limit of 100 permits 1000 spans, and a configured limit of 2000 silently loses spans above 1000 that were previously accepted. Pass the configured limit into the eviction script rather than leaving the public configuration disconnected from enforcement."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 63,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Protect the root span during eviction",
      "body": "ZPOPMIN treats the root span like any other timestamp-scored payload. If enough children end after the root, or share its timestamp and sort after its serialized payload, pruning can remove the root. The has-root marker nevertheless remains true, so the segment receives the short root timeout but flushes without any span marked is_segment and loses the root payload. Preserve the root during truncation, and cover equal timestamps and children ending after the root in eviction tests."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Guard requests without an organization membership
findings.body: Organization-scoped API authentication can authorize this endpoint without attaching a user membership, leaving organization_context.member as None. The new expression dereferences that member for non-superusers, even when optimized_pagination was not requested. Previously working audit-log requests using organization API authentication will therefore return an AttributeError/500. Handle absent memberships and evaluate the optimization gate only for opt-in requests.

findings.title: Use datetime-aware cursor conversion for audit logs
findings.body: OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint selects OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", but get_item_key passes the AuditLogEntry datetime value to math.floor/math.ceil. Building cursors for any nonempty first page therefore raises TypeError. The inverse conversion also returns a raw numeric cursor value instead of the datetime required by the query. Inherit or reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new audit-log pagination path works.

findings.title: Do not pass negative offsets to QuerySet slicing
findings.body: The advanced-pagination branch passes a negative cursor offset directly into a Django QuerySet slice. Django explicitly rejects negative slice bounds rather than interpreting them as reverse pagination, so an enabled request with a cursor such as 0:-1:0 raises an exception before fetching any rows. Implement reverse pagination using ordering and nonnegative bounds, or reject unsupported offsets with a controlled pagination error.

findings.title: Migrate or version the Redis buffer keyspace
findings.body: This replaces Redis sets with sorted sets while retaining the existing span-buf:s:* key names. Live buffers written by the old consumer remain ordinary sets, so ZADD, ZCARD, and ZSCAN will raise WRONGTYPE after deployment. Failed processing batches cannot advance their Kafka offsets, and old and new consumers are mutually incompatible during a rolling upgrade. Introduce a compatible migration/drain strategy or a versioned buffer namespace before switching command types.

findings.title: Preserve timestamp scores when merging span buffers
findings.body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. When the same payload is present in both buffers—for example, a replayed grandchild written under its parent after an earlier batch moved it to the root—its end-timestamp score is added to the existing score. An old span can consequently receive a score far beyond every real timestamp and survive eviction while newer spans are removed. Use a score-preserving aggregation such as AGGREGATE MAX for both unions.

findings.title: Honor the configured maximum segment span count
findings.body: The eviction threshold is hard-coded to 1000, while the Python flush-time check has been removed and SpansBuffer still exposes max_segment_spans. That constructor argument now has no effect: a configured limit of 100 permits 1000 spans, and a configured limit of 2000 silently loses spans above 1000 that were previously accepted. Pass the configured limit into the eviction script rather than leaving the public configuration disconnected from enforcement.

findings.title: Protect the root span during eviction
findings.body: ZPOPMIN treats the root span like any other timestamp-scored payload. If enough children end after the root, or share its timestamp and sort after its serialized payload, pruning can remove the root. The has-root marker nevertheless remains true, so the segment receives the short root timeout but flushes without any span marked is_segment and loses the root payload. Preserve the root during truncation, and cover equal timestamps and children ending after the root in eviction tests.
